clue.text: Desire to attract attention characteristic of successful artists?

definitions.meaning: a compulsion to show off and be noticed
read literally, a successful artist is one who gets many shows of their work in galleries

explanation.surface: A show-off streak is what marks out the artists who make it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a craving for notice, and also, taken word by word, the state of being much put on show, as a celebrated painter is.

clue.text: Showing the attraction of current action?

definitions.text: Showing the attraction of current action?

parts.words: Showing the attraction of current action?
parts.note: current is electrical current, and the attraction is the magnetic pull an electric current produces

explanation.surface: Something displays the appeal of what is happening right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire carrying current behaves as a magnet, so the pull it exerts is the field physics names for electricity and magnetism together.

clue.text: Regular visitor somewhat put in the shade

indicators.note: the words for somewhat are placed inside the word for the shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps coming round finds themselves rather overshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in the shade' reads as one idiom meaning outshone, but it splits: 'put in' is the container signal and 'the shade' is HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual frequenter of a place, such as a café regular, is its constant caller.

clue.text: One goes over the top in battle

definitions.meaning: a knitted hood pulled over the head, the top of the body
the 1854 Crimean War battle, famous for the Charge of the Light Brigade

explanation.surface: A soldier climbs out of the trench into the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' suggests soldiers leaving a trench to attack; here the top is the head, which the woollen hood covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The woollen head covering takes its name from the Crimean battle where British troops wore them against the cold.

clue.text: Having had will to put up gallery

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for put is written bottom to top

parts.note: to put is to set
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone with a legacy plan sets about building an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, with the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid legal document leaving their estate is described by this legal term.

clue.text: Modern works some love initially

indicators.note: initially places the letter for love at the front of the charade

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
some means a part

explanation.surface: Some contemporary pieces are adored at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s style of abstract optical-illusion painting is a body of recent artworks.

clue.text: Ran through one barrier in Maryland

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the word for barrier is placed inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: MD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maryland
a pale is a fence or boundary stake

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted through a single fence in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' looks like the runner's action, but it is the definition in the sense of pierced with a sword or spike.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone through is to pierce them, as with a stake or sword thrust.

clue.text: Taken wrongly? Is suitable when covered by doctor

indicators.note: the pieces for is suitable sit inside the abbreviation for a doctor, which covers them

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
suitable means apt or appropriate

explanation.surface: A medic checks whether something was stolen or merely suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds that have been embezzled or used dishonestly have been seized without right.

clue.text: Laboratory, in some century, returned old instruments

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters built so far is read backwards
the short word for laboratory goes inside the word some

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for century, from Latin centum

explanation.surface: A laboratory in some past age gave back antique musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole of SOLABME plus C into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are harpsichords, keyboard instruments of the baroque era, cembalo being the Italian name.

clue.text: Put together a piano model

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a piano and a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To set one thing beside another, placing them side by side, is a formal verb for juxtaposing.

clue.text: French comic in short scene, not at all moving

indicators.note: the comic's name sits inside the abbreviated scene

parts.note: sc is the abbreviation for scene in a script
Jacques Tati was the French comic actor and director of Monsieur Hulot films

explanation.surface: A French comedian in a brief sketch fails to stir the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at all moving' reads as a dull performance, but means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary, without any motion, is fixed in place.

clue.text: Unusually open late for big game

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of open late are put into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A shop opens late for the big match, which is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests a match; here it means large animals hunted on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game is large wild animals hunted for sport, and this horned African grazer is one.

clue.text: One of eight religious leaders in 1518? Just the opposite

definitions.text: One of eight religious leaders in 1518? Just the opposite

parts.words: One of eight religious leaders in 1518? Just the opposite
parts.note: 1518 is not a year but entries 15 and 18; one of eight pontiffs who shared a name is that poet's two names in the opposite order

explanation.surface: A pontiff of the Renaissance year 1518 is described, then reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 1518 looks like a year in the Renaissance papacy, but it points to entries 15 and 18: swap the two words of that poet's name and you get a title held by eight popes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight Roman pontiffs took this papal name, the last in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: See 12
Colonial language from Asia Frank translated

indicators.note: translated suggests putting into another form, so the letters of Asia Frank are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Frank translates from an Asian tongue into a colonial one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch-derived tongue of South Africa developed among settlers in the Cape Colony.

clue.text: Russian emperor meeting popular European poet

parts.note: three Russian tsars were called Alexander
pop is short for popular

explanation.surface: A tsar meets a well-loved writer from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century English satirist wrote The Rape of the Lock in heroic couplets.

clue.text: Siren I installed in centre after N D disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs the combined letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A temptress is placed at the heart of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The N D in the printed clue reads as an OCR slip for 'a'; the wordplay needs only I and CENTRE, shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman who lures others, a temptress or lure.

clue.text: Departs this country miming way to rise in noble status

parts.note: d is the timetable abbreviation for departs
UK is the United Kingdom, home of this newspaper

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for way is written bottom to top

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: Someone leaves Britain to climb the aristocratic ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to rise' reads as a route upward, but 'to rise' turns MODE into EDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank held by a duke, the highest grade of the British peerage, is a noble title.

clue.text: See 15
For informer, a way to make fair adjustments

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a rat is an informer who betrays associates

explanation.surface: A method of fair settlement suits a police grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportional sharing, dividing costs in line with each party's stake, is the Latin phrase for equitable division.

clue.text: Single-minded contribution to recording

definitions.meaning: obsessively focused on a sole interest
a single number on an album or tape

explanation.surface: An obsessive musician adds one song to the album.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a mind that runs on a sole rail, and also, literally, a lone song on a record.

clue.text: Primates going round southern parts of church

indicators.note: the word for primates surrounds the letter for southern

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: Monkeys run round the southern end of a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the rounded recesses at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Nuts in biscuit, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than seen, giving a soundalike

parts.note: a cookie is the American name for a biscuit

explanation.surface: A biscuit with nuts in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an ingredient of the biscuit; it is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eccentric or crazy, a bit mad, is called nuts in slang.

clue.text: What's in store as punishment

definitions.meaning: goods a shop holds, its inventory
the wooden frame in which offenders were once locked by the ankles for public humiliation

explanation.surface: What is coming is a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's supplies are its holdings of goods, and the old pillory-like frame was a penalty for petty crime.

clue.text: Judge in African capital thanks another in Asia

indicators.note: the letter for judge goes inside the name of the capital

parts.note: Dakar is the capital of Senegal
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A magistrate in a West African city gives thanks for another posting in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another capital, following 'African capital': this is an older spelling of Jakarta, Indonesia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian seat of government is a second capital city, this time on the Asian continent.

clue.text: Brief festive writing of Noel Coward ignore pained expression

parts.note: Noel is a name for the Yuletide festival

indicators.note: ignore tells us to leave out the letters of the pained cry from the word coward

parts.note: taken as written
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A short seasonal note from the playwright Noel Coward, minus a wince.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright's name is the misdirection: his first name is the season of Christmas, and his surname is cut down by 'ignore', which drops a wince from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short seasonal greeting sent by post is a brief piece of holiday correspondence.
